panels.title: Chat requests/sec by operation
panels.description: Recorded series kb:chat_requests:rate5m. Includes cancelled requests: a cancellation is traffic, it is just not a failure. This is also the traffic-floor term in KbChatErrorRateHigh.

panels.title: Chat error + timeout ratio
panels.description: Recorded series kb:chat_error_ratio:5m — the ONE definition of an error rate. It counts outcome=error AND outcome=timeout and excludes outcome=cancelled. Never re-derive this matcher in a panel: a panel written against outcome=error alone reads 0.4% during an outage in which a third of requests time out. Absent rather than zero before the first failure.

panels.title: First visible token, p95 by model (seconds)
panels.description: THE SLO NUMBER: measured from Laravel's receipt of the client request to the first token event flushed to the client, so it contains the retrieval leg. docs/17 §23 targets 4 s, which is why 4 is a bucket edge. Do not substitute kb_provider_first_token_seconds — that starts at the provider call and hides the 1.5 s retrieval budget entirely.

panels.title: Chat duration, p95 by outcome (seconds)
panels.description: Split by outcome so a fast failure cannot flatter the percentile. `le` is kept alongside the grouping label in every quantile here: aggregating it away first leaves no buckets to interpolate and histogram_quantile returns nonsense.

panels.title: Open SSE streams
panels.description: Capacity headroom. A monotonic climb that never returns to baseline is a leaked finalizer — a streaming span or generator that was not closed in a finally — not organic growth.

panels.title: Cancellation rate
panels.description: Tracked separately from the error rate on purpose: a user hanging up is not our failure, and folding it in makes alarms fire during a normal demo. A cancelled stream still finalizes usage, because the provider billed the tokens it had already generated.

panels.title: Model fallbacks
panels.description: A silent fallback looks like the primary model produced the answer, and the eval suite then scores the wrong model. error_class carries the trigger.

panels.title: Answers by finish_reason
panels.description: Insufficient-evidence and truncation rates. Values are the SSE terminal finish_reason enum. The insufficient-evidence rate is a PRODUCT number and is deliberately not alerted on — a refusal on thin evidence is the system working.
